DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilq.qov.ph DILG OPINION NO. 01 S. 2022 January 7, 2022 Dir. MARIA KRISTINA E. CASSION Executive Director Regional Franchising and Regulatory Office No. 13 Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board LTFRB CARAGA Regional Office DOTr Regional Complex Brgy. Ampayon, Butuan City Dear Dir. Cassion: This refers to your letter dated October 22, 2021, through the Memorandum dated II November 2021 from Dir. Vivian P. Suansing, OIC, BLGS, seeking clarification concerning the legality of the "Dispatching Fee" collected from operators and/or drivers of Public Utility Vehicles (PUV) by a certain Mr. Irenio Ajos Sr. (Mr. Ajos) at Tandag City Overland Transport Terminal (TCOTT). Per the letter, CARAGA Federation of Transport Service Cooperatives (CARFEDTRANSCO) raised during a meeting with Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) CARAGA that Mr. Ajos had been collecting a Dispatching Fee (DF) from PUVs utilizing the TCOTT at Surigao del Sur. The DF is paid on top of the terminal fee collected by the local govemment units (LGUs). According to the drivers and operators, Mr. Ajos would collect the fare directly from the passengers, and automatically deduct the ten per centum (10%) DF before transmitting the remainder to the PUV driver and operator. In your Letter, Mr. Ajos presents to the drivers and operators a Mayor's Permit issued by Hon. Roxanne Pimentel (Mayor Pimentel), Mayor of Tandag City, Surigao del Sur. The Mayor's Permit allegedly authorizes him to collect the DF. Mr. Ajos further claims that he is a trusted person of Mayor Pimentel. On October 22, 2021, your good office sent a letter of same date to Mayor Pimentel, copy fumished DILG CARAGA, requesting for a clarification on the allegations of the PUV drivers and operators. DILG CARAGA, in a Memorandum dated October 25, 2021 , likewise required DILG Provincial Office for Surigao del Sur and Tandag City CLGOO to obtain a written comment from Mayor Pimentel on the matter. As of date, this level has not been furnished any response by Mayor Pimentel, if any. "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

This Department respectfully submits that LGUs may, through an ordinance, require a dispatcher to be present at public terminals who shall be entitled to a reasonable fee for their services. Verily, this Department concurs with the action of DILG CARAGA which ultimately requires a response from Mayor Pimentel to confirm the facts and circumstances surrounding the complaint of the PUV drivers and operators. Corollary thereto, an independent investigation may likewise be conducted to verify whether the City of Tandag has an ordinance authorizing a dispatcher to collect the DF. Republic Act No. 7160, othem'ise known as the Local Govemment Code (LGC) provides that municipalities and cities are authorized to establish and regulate PUV terminals within their territorial jurisdiction, to wit: Section 447. Powers, Duties, Functions and Compensation. - (a) The sangguniang bayan, as the legislative body of the municipality, shall enact ordinances, approve resolutions and appropriate funds for the general welfare of the municipality and its inhabitants pursuant to Section 16 of this Code and in the proper exercise of the corporate powers of the municipality as provided for under Section 22 of this Code, and shall: xxxx (5) Approve ordinances which shall ensure the efficient and effective delivery of the basic services and facilities as provided for under Section 17 of this Code, and in addition to said services and facilities, shall: xxxx (v) Regulate the use of streets, avenues, alleys, sidewalks, bridges, parks and other public places and approve the construction, improvement, repair and maintenance of the same; establish bus and vehicle stops and terminals or regulate the use of the same by privately- owned vehicles which serve the public; regulate garages and the operation of conveyances for hire; designate stands to be occupied by public vehicles when not in use; regulate the putting up of signs, signposts, awnings and awning posts on the streets; provide for the lighting, cleaning and sprinkling of streets and public places; xxxx" Section 458. Powers, Duties, Functions and Compensation. (a) The sangguniang panlungsod, as the legislative body of the city, shall enact ordinances, approve resolutions and appropriate funds for the general welfare of the city and its inhabitants pursuant to Section 16 of this Code and in the proper exercise of the corporate powers of the city as provided for under Section 22 of this Code, and shal:xxxx (5) Approve ordinances which shall ensure the efficient and effective delivery of the basic services and facilities as provided for under Section 17 of this Code, and in addition to said services and facilities, shall:xxxx (v) (v) Regulate the use of streets, avenues, alleys, sidewalks, bridges, parks and other public places and approve the construction, improvement repair and maintenance Of the same; establish bus and vehicle stops and terminals or regulate the use of the same by privately- owned vehicles which serve the public; regulate garages and the operation of conveyances for hire; designate stands to be occupied by public vehicles when not in use; regulate the putting up of signs, signposts, awnings and awning posts on the streets; and provide for the lighting, cleaning and sprinkling of streets; and public places;;xxxx" Meanwhile, Department Order No. 2008-23 dated 16 June 2008 issued by then Department of Transportation and Communication, now the Department of Transportation (DOTr DO 2008-23) provides that: "Section 6. Imposition of Other Local Fees and Charges Affecting Public Transport Operation. page 2 Of 4

As a general rule, the LGUs should desist from unilaterally increasing fees and charges that would contribute to higher public transport costs. Increases in fees and charges should be in coordination with the LTFRB and should be commensurate with the administrative expenses. Before changes in fees can be imposed, there must be a public hearing and publication in local newspapers of general circulation and/or posting in at least four (4) conspicuous and publicly accessible places including the main entrance of the city/ municipal hall prior to said imposition." The laws and guidelines are therefore consistent that an ordinance is required before an LGU may impose a regulation upon a transport terminal. Additionally, DOTr DO 2008-23 requires that any increase in the imposed fees and charges which shall contribute to higher public transportation cost must be: (a) coordinated with the Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board; (b) publicly heard; and (c) posted in at least four (4) conspicuous and publicly accessible places in the LGU. Based on the foregoing, cities and municipalities, such as Tandag City, have the authority to regulate transport terminals within its jurisdiction and, in furtherance thereof, may require a dispatching officer to staff the same. The dispatching officer may be tasked to take charge in scheduling/dispatching PUVs and organizing passengers. A reasonable amount may thereafter be paid to the dispatching officer as payment for their services. The imposition of a dispatching officer, however, must be made through an ordinance duly passed by the local sanggunian. Additionally, when the payment for the dispatching officer's services entails higher public transportation cost, then the procedure under DOTr DO 2008-23 must be followed by the LGU. The LGC further provides as follows: "Section 77. Responsibility for Human Resources and Development. - The chief executive of every local govemment unit shall be responsible for human resources and development in his unit and shall take all personnel actions in accordance with the Constitutional provisions on civil service, pertinent laws, and rules and regulations thereon, including such policies, guidelines and standards as the Civil Service Commission may establish: Provided, That the local chief executive may employ emergency or casual employees or laborers paid on a daily wage or piecework basis and hired through job orders for local projects authorized by the sanggunian concerned, without need of approval or attestation by the Civil Service Commission: Provided, further, That the period of employment of emergency or casual laborers as provided in this Section shall not exceed six (6) months.. Section 87. Disciplinary Jurisdiction. - Except as otherwise provided by law, the local chief executive may impose the penalty of removal from service, demotion in rank, suspension for not more than one (1) year without pay, fine in an amount not exceeding six (6) months salary, or reprimand and otherwise discipline subordinate officials and employees under his jurisdiction. If the penalty imposed is suspension without pay for not more than thirty (30) days, his decision shall be final. If the penalty imposed is heavier than suspension of thirty (30) days, the decision shall be appealable to the Civil Service Commission, which shall decide the appeal within thirty (30) days from receipt thereof." Assuming an ordinance indeed mandates a dispatching officer's presence at a public terminal, any administrative complaints against them shall be under the jurisdiction of the local chief executive, such as a mayor. Page 3 of 4

Verily, DILG CARAGA was correct to exact an explanation from Hon. Pimentel as regards the present complaint against a certain Mr. Ajos who claims to be an authorized dispatching officer. DILG CARAGA is, however, not precluded from initiating a separate investigation to confirm whether an ordinance covering TOCTT exists which may prevent undue delay in addressing the concems of the PUV drivers and/or operators. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the COLINS. We hope to have sufficiently addressed your concems. Thank you. BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: GAN Underse tary for Local Govemment cc: Dir.
